clue.text: We leave waitress organising apples and pears

indicators.note: organising puts things into a fresh order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to leave is to go away, so the first pair of words departs from the longer word

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to remove
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stops a waitress from sorting out the fruit display.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing W and E from WAITRESS leaves AITRSS to rearrange. 'Apples and pears' is Cockney rhyming slang, a London habit of replacing a word with a phrase that rhymes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang the phrase rhymes with the word it replaces, so the fruit pair stands for flights of steps.

clue.text: Whistle-blower's story about Archer?

parts.note: William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer who shot an apple from his son's head
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Someone who exposes wrongdoing tells a story about a person named Archer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'story about Archer' as a story about the archer: Tell's tale. The question mark warns that Archer is an example, William Tell, and 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reports others' misdeeds to authority is called a telltale, much like an informer exposing wrongdoing.

clue.text: Meet some splinter section

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of letters lying inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words, dropping the outer ones

explanation.surface: Members of a breakaway faction gather for a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or roads that cross each other are said to meet at the point where they cross.

clue.text: Endless fruit for Muslim ruler

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the next word is cut off

parts.note: a sultana is a dried grape

explanation.surface: A never-ending supply of fruit is laid on for a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is used for the sovereign of various Islamic states, such as Oman or Brunei.

clue.text: After Betfred ruined me, finally back in the black

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the letters of the company name are scrambled

parts.note: Betfred is a British chain of betting shops, taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter only of the word just before it

parts.note: the last letter of me

explanation.surface: A gambler whose bookmaker cleaned them out has finally paid everything off.
explanation.walkthrough: Betfred is a big British bookmaker, so the surface tells a gambling story; its letters with the E from 'me' rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the black means having a positive balance; returning there means owing nothing to anyone.

clue.text: The elder Trojans revised old farewell texts

indicators.note: a revised version has been reworked, so the three words' letters are rewritten in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Older citizens of Troy rewrote some ancient goodbye messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a letter is a written message from a partner ending the relationship, famously sent to soldiers abroad.

clue.text: Roof of bus station rebuilt for plant expert

indicators.note: in a down entry the roof is the top, so just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of bus

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again differently, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bus station's roof is renovated to suit someone who studies greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who specialises in the study of vegetation and flowers is a specialist in botany.

clue.text: Fast ships

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a navy's group of vessels

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of speedy vessels, but each word is its own meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a literary adjective for swift movement and also a noun for a body of naval vessels.

clue.text: Spectacular Rise of Popeye — dropping second half

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom upwards, so the name is turned round

parts.note: the spinach-eating cartoon sailor, taken as written

indicators.note: only the second half of the following word survives, its first half thrown away

parts.note: taken as written; its last four letters are kept

explanation.surface: A dramatic headline about the cartoon sailor's rise and his ratings dropping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like an instruction to delete something; here it is simply the word whose back half, PING, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astonishing enough to make your eyes bulge is striking, impressive and sensational.

clue.text: Little 7 is poorly accommodated in a loft conversion

indicators.note: to be accommodated in a place is to be housed inside it, so one piece sits within the other
a loft conversion remodels the space, so these letters are refashioned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
feeling poorly is being ill

explanation.surface: Someone small and unwell is badly housed in a converted attic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little 7' sends you to 7-down, FLEET; a little fleet is the answer. 'Poorly' looks like an adverb but means ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A small group of ships or boats is a diminutive naval force, the word coming from Spanish for a small fleet.

clue.text: Draw shade in layers

parts.note: a draw in sport is a tie
red is a shade, or colour

explanation.surface: An artist sketches and shades with built-up layers of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' and 'shade' read as art instructions; they are a sporting result and a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged in rows or levels one above another, like a wedding cake built in stacked stages.

clue.text: Crossing Jordan almost spoiled by sycophancy

indicators.note: something spoiled has been messed up, so the surviving letters are jumbled
almost all of the name is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: the country, or river, taken as written
unction is an excessive, oily show of earnestness or flattery

explanation.surface: A trip across the River Jordan is nearly ruined by fawning hangers-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing Jordan' looks like a single phrase about the river; Crossing alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where two or more streets meet or cross over is a crossroads, a kind of intersection.

clue.text: Young kangaroo who may now be holder of a bus pass

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: a boomer is a large male kangaroo, so its infant

definitions.text: who may now be holder of a bus pass
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone born in the post-war birth surge, now old enough for free travel

explanation.walkthrough: A boomer is Australian slang for a big male kangaroo. In Britain, pensioners get a free bus pass, which the post-1945 generation is now reaching.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a person born during the population surge after the Second World War, now reaching pension age.

clue.text: Starting point for Swiss city lacking top wine

indicators.note: lacking its top means the drink's first letter is missing

parts.note: Basel is a city in northern Switzerland on the Rhine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Swiss city tour begins somewhere that has run out of good wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference level from which progress or change is measured is the initial benchmark for comparison.

clue.text: What may be banned in summer is tights and slippers accompaniment

definitions.text: What may be banned in summer

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or tights
pipe and slippers is the traditional picture of a cosy evening at home

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which summer clothing gets banned: tights, slippers, and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: In dry British summers water companies impose a hosepipe ban, forbidding garden watering. 'Pipe and slippers' is a stock image of a man relaxing at home.
explanation.definitionFit: During droughts British water firms forbid using garden watering tubes, so this item is what a summer ban targets.

clue.text: Look back in despair, suffering as Britain is now

indicators.note: back means the short word for look is read from end to start
suffering suggests being in a bad state, so the combined letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: lo, as in 'lo and behold', means look
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone looks back in despair at how Britain is suffering at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look back in despair' echoes the play Look Back in Anger. The definition describes the country's divided state since Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation sharply split into two opposing camps, as after the Brexit vote, is described as divided into extremes.

clue.text: Bum smoothing cream at first new in make-up

indicators.note: in means one letter is placed inside the cosmetic
at first points to the opening letters of the two words just before it

parts.note: the first letter of smoothing
the first letter of cream
rouge is a red cosmetic for the cheeks
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A beauty routine: new cream applied to smooth the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' looks like the British slang for buttocks, which suits the cream; here it is a verb meaning to cadge.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum a cigarette or a lift is to cadge it, getting something free by begging or sponging.

clue.text: Slimy act represented as 'spiritual'

indicators.note: represented means presented afresh, so the letters are set out in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant behaviour is passed off as a matter of the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the soul, religious mysteries or hidden truths beyond ordinary understanding is otherworldly and mystic.

clue.text: See 13
Promise onboard weapons

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel
to give your word is to promise

explanation.surface: A pledge that arms are carried on the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Being on board means being inside the ship, SS, so the promise sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Long bladed hand weapons used for cutting and thrusting, such as sabres and rapiers, are arms.

clue.text: Half contribute to lower building, which is critical to airport operations

definitions.text: which is critical to airport operations
definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing in for the noun

indicators.note: only half of the following word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: taken as written; its first five letters are kept

indicators.note: building means constructing something new, so those letters are assembled in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plea to chip in towards a lower building that matters to how an airport runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' looks like the noun being defined; it is the instruction to rearrange 'to lower'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall structure housing air traffic controllers directs every take-off and landing, so airports cannot run without it.

clue.text: President's bottom, bottom President

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the last letter, so only the end of the first word is used

parts.note: the last letter of the first President
the rump is the bottom, or backside

explanation.surface: A crude jibe about a US president, calling him a backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated words do different jobs: the first 'bottom' selects a letter, the second means backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump served as the forty-fifth and forty-seventh holder of the United States' highest office.

clue.text: See 2
Attack one politician with a plastic gun

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: plastic material can be moulded into any shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: a Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: An assault on a politician carried out with a toy gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like it describes the gun; it tells you to rearrange its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn someone's motives is to challenge or dispute them verbally, calling them into question.

clue.text: How to get to Brussels? Possibly, routes are endless

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible versions, so the letters may be reordered
endless means the final letter of the preceding word is cut away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller asking the way to Belgium's capital hears the routes are countless.
explanation.walkthrough: Eurostar is the high-speed train through the Channel Tunnel linking London with Paris and Brussels.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-Channel rail service runs direct trains from London, so it is a way of reaching Belgium's capital.

clue.text: Listened to musicians' covers

parts.note: rappers are hip-hop musicians; the W is silent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' suggests cover versions of songs, but it is the definition: paper or plastic packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper or plastic sheets used to enclose sweets or parcels serve as protective packaging around them.

clue.text: Bugger study — it's very wet

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry on finding the study flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: As exclamations, 'bugger' and 'sod' are interchangeable British expletives.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaked through with water, like a lawn after heavy rain, is saturated and drenched.
